topic: Frankland Centre and Dryandra Ward occupancy, 2021–2025
question: I refer to the 30-bed Frankland Forensic Centre and the 15-bed Dryandra Ward, and I ask: (a) What was the occupancy rate for each centre for each of the following years: (i) 2021; (ii) 2022; (iii) 2023; (iv) 2024; and (v) 2025 to date?
answer_summary: Frankland Centre ran at 94–97% occupancy every year from 2021 to 2025 (30 operational beds throughout). Dryandra Ward's governance transferred to the State Forensic Mental Health Service on 31 July 2023; from that date its occupancy ran 66–76% against 8.7–12.2 average operational beds (of a 15-bed capacity). The answer notes forensic consumers under CLMI Act 2023 Custody Orders may have legally mandated overnight leave for up to 13 of 14 nights, which affects how occupancy is recorded.

topic: People needing forensic mental health care held in prison instead
question: Since the commencement of WA's new Criminal Law (Mental Impairment) Act 2023 in September 2024, how many people with a mental impairment deemed suitable for care in a forensic facility are currently incarcerated in the WA prison system?
answer_summary: 15 people deemed suitable for care in a forensic mental health facility were, at the time of answering, held in the WA prison system instead — a direct capacity/demand data point.

question: Since the commencement of WA's new Criminal Law (Mental Impairment) Act 2023 in September 2024, how many people with a mental impairment deemed suitable for care in a forensic facility are currently incarcerated in the WA prison system?
